| 0x730D | Cold Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when coolant temperature hasn't breached the proper threshold. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x730D | Cold Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x740D | High Octane Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when high-octane fuel is determined. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x740D | High Octane Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x750D | High Detonation Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when high-detonation is occurring. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. Make sure that this map's values are lower than the high octane map's values. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x750D | High Detonation Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x768D | MBT Flame Speed Map — Laminar flow flame velocity basic map | 4×4 uint8 | Laminar Flame Speed (cc/ms), value = x*0.0625 | Ignition Timing / MBT Calculation |
| 0x769D | Cylinder Fresh Air Rate Map — "Fresh Air Rate Map" OR "Freshness Ratio Map". Sets wvITAN (and vITAN), which is used in MBT calculations. | 4×4 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Ignition Timing / MBT Calculation |
| 0x76AD | Acceleration Fuel Compensation Map — Multiplied by mVOLR, Engine RPM, and 55 (unscaled) to set vCFL "FLOAD Basic Value" | 8×8 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Transient Correction |
| 0x76ED | Deceleration Fuel Compensation Map — Multiplied by mVOLR, Engine RPM, and 55 (unscaled) to set vCFL "FLOAD Basic Value" | 8×8 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Transient Correction |
| 0x786D | Fuel Compensation Map (16x16) — This map will directly trim Base Fuel Schedule. Given how we have transient throttle fuel compensation maps, this map is really designed for steady state conditions with little RPM deviance. However, you can use this map to tune for transient conditions. View it similarly to STFT's in a way. But as a preset trimming value rather than reacting to AFR deviances. | 16×16 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Main |
| 0x79FD | Target AFR Map (8x8) — This map will be directly influence fueling. Any cells that are set to 14.7 AFR will have the ECU run in closed-loop mode. | 0x8108 | AFR Correction Map (Bank 2) — This value is added on top of the AFR value from the AFR Conversion Table. | 8×8 uint16 | AFR Adjustment (AFR), value = (x*0.002)-65.536 | Diagnostics / Oxygen Sensor Calibration / Wideband O2 Sensor / Main |

| 0x8C88 | Engine Torque Map — Map value is compensated, then sent to the TCM for it to determine proper line pressure. Raising the values will result in increased line pressure, while decreasing the values will result in decreased line pressure. It's important to ensure that the map values are at LEAST equal to actual torque output. While it's safe to specify higher torque figures than what you're making, it's extremely dangerous to specify lower torque figures than what you're making. | 16×16 uint16 | Engine Torque (lb-ft), value = x*0.073756-2416.836136 | Transmission / Shifting Performance |
| 0x8E88 | Knock Slice Map — This table sets the thresholds for determining knock by cylinder. If the knock strength value exceeds this map value, then it adds one to the knock count. For built motors, you'll need to raise these values so that it doesn't count false knock as actual knock. | 16×6 uint16 | Knock Strength Threshold (%), value = x*0.0015259 | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Thresholds |

| 0x652D | Fuel Injector Latency Adder — This is the value in milliseconds that is added to the injector latency 14V table for every 1v drop in voltage. IE: if latency at 14v is 2ms and the adder is 1ms then the latency at 13v would be 3ms. | 1 uint8 | ms/V, value = x*0.000976563 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x6740 | Closed Loop to Open Loop Delay — "All the delay stage delays" This value represents a maximum delay between the time the car goes from closed to open loop fuel target values. There are several other potential delays but setting this to 0 should override them. For performance applications to ensure that the ecu transitions to the fuel target as fast as possible upon wide open throttle, set to 0. | 1 uint8 | Seconds, value = x*0.2 | Fuel Delivery / Air Fuel Ratio / Delays |
| 0x691F | MAF Factor — Used in main fuel calc, can be used instead of adjusting K factor. This is what Nissan uses to scale MAF from factory. | 1 uint8 | scaling "kg/hr (x*0.0001)" | Airflow / Main |
| 0x6B40 | Fuel Injector Latency at 14V | 1 uint8 | ms, value = x*0.01 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x6DC0 | APO Threshold (Brake) — The APO threshold you need to breach in order to trigger the TVO limiter when the brake is currently being applied. Raising this threshold above ~83 degrees will allow you to bypass this TVO limiter. | 1 uint16 | Degrees, value = x*0.11 | Electronic Throttle Control / Accelerator Pedal / Limiters |
| 0x6F24 | K-Value — Air volume pulse width conversion constant. Represents a fuel injector factor. | 1 uint16 | ms/kg, raw value | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x6FA8 | Rev Limit (Fuel Cut - 3D) — These are the engine speeds at which the fuel cut rev limiter is engaged and disengaged. ## AC31A · 2004 Infiniti G35 AWD · ECUID 1AC31C · SH7058 · 1024kb

| Address | Controls | Layout | Values mean | Category |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x652D | Fuel Injector Latency Adder — This is the value in milliseconds that is added to the injector latency 14V table for every 1v drop in voltage. IE: if latency at 14v is 2ms and the adder is 1ms then the latency at 13v would be 3ms. | 1 uint8 | ms/V, value = x*0.000976563 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x6740 | Closed Loop to Open Loop Delay — "All the delay stage delays" This value represents a maximum delay between the time the car goes from closed to open loop fuel target values. There are several other potential delays but setting this to 0 should override them. For performance applications to ensure that the ecu transitions to the fuel target as fast as possible upon wide open throttle, set to 0. | 1 uint8 | Seconds, value = x*0.2 | Fuel Delivery / Air Fuel Ratio / Delays |
| 0x68FD | Flags 24 | 1 uint8 |  |  |
| 0x691F | MAF Factor — Used in main fuel calc, can be used instead of adjusting K factor. This is what Nissan uses to scale MAF from factory. | 1 uint8 | scaling "kg/hr (x*0.0001)" | Airflow / Main |
| 0x697A | Radiator Fan High Coolant | 1 uint8 |  |  |
| 0x6B40 | Fuel Injector Latency at 14V | 1 uint8 | ms, value = x*0.01 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x6C18 | Speed Limiter (Fuel Cut) — Primarily used in automatics. It's the speed at which fuel cut will occur. It's normally set above the throttle cut speed limiter, so you're unlikely to ever hit this stock. | 1 uint8 | Vehicle Speed (MPH), value = x*1.24300808 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x6C24 | Speed Limiter (Fuel Restore) — Ensure that this value is below the fuel cut speed limiter's value. | 1 uint8 | Vehicle Speed (MPH), value = x*1.24300808 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x6DC0 | APO Threshold (Brake) — The APO threshold you need to breach in order to trigger the TVO limiter when the brake is currently being applied. Raising this threshold above ~83 degrees will allow you to bypass this TVO limiter. | 1 uint16 | Degrees, value = x*0.11 | Electronic Throttle Control / Accelerator Pedal / Limiters |
| 0x6F24 | K-Value — Air volume pulse width conversion constant. Represents a fuel injector factor. | 1 uint16 | ms/kg, raw value | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x6FA8 | Rev Limit (Fuel Cut - 3D) — These are the engine speeds at which the fuel cut rev limiter is engaged and disengaged. When engine speed is equal to or exceeds the 'On' value, fuel cut is active, after which, if engine speed drops below the 'Off' value, fueling is resumed. | 2×2 uint16 | Engine Speed (RPM), value = x*12.5 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Cut / Main |
| 0x7036 | Throttle Rev Limiter — Engine speed at which the throttle rev limiter is engaged and disengaged. | 1 uint16 | RPM, value = x*0.78125 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x705E | Speed Limiter — The speed at which throttle cut occurs. For automatics, be sure to change the fuel cut speed limiters as well. | 1 uint16 | MPH, value = x*0.0621371 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x707C | Minimum Injector Pulse Width — This is the minimum pulsewidth the injectors will run at. (Excluding fuel cut) | 1 uint16 | ms, value = x*0.00390625 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x70A8 | Cylinder Filling Up Efficiency Scaler — BFS at which maximum airflow occurs. This value is used to setup ITAC as an estimated Volumetric Efficiency value. So if BFS=BFS Scaler, Cylinder Filling Up Efficiency = 100%. This CAN go above 100%, so ensure that you're never going over this value by too much. | 1 uint16 | ms, value = x*0.000488281 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x70F0 | MAF Idle Voltage Limits — This is the voltage range the ECU expects to see from the MAF sensor at idle. | 2 uint16 | V, value = x*0.005 | Idle Speed Control / Limiters / General Limiters |
| 0x71EC | Checksum XOR word | uint32 | nisckfix recomputes this after any edit | Checksum |
| 0x71F4 | Checksum SUM word | uint32 | nisckfix recomputes this after any edit | Checksum |
| 0x730D | Cold Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when coolant temperature hasn't breached the proper threshold. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x730D | Cold Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x740D | High Octane Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when high-octane fuel is determined. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x740D | High Octane Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x750D | High Detonation Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when high-detonation is occurring. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. Make sure that this map's values are lower than the high octane map's values. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x750D | High Detonation Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x768D | MBT Flame Speed Map — Laminar flow flame velocity basic map | 4×4 uint8 | Laminar Flame Speed (cc/ms), value = x*0.0625 | Ignition Timing / MBT Calculation |
| 0x769D | Cylinder Fresh Air Rate Map — "Fresh Air Rate Map" OR "Freshness Ratio Map". Sets wvITAN (and vITAN), which is used in MBT calculations. | 4×4 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Ignition Timing / MBT Calculation |
| 0x76AD | Acceleration Fuel Compensation Map — Multiplied by mVOLR, Engine RPM, and 55 (unscaled) to set vCFL "FLOAD Basic Value" | 8×8 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Transient Correction |
| 0x76ED | Deceleration Fuel Compensation Map — Multiplied by mVOLR, Engine RPM, and 55 (unscaled) to set vCFL "FLOAD Basic Value" | 8×8 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Transient Correction |
| 0x786D | Fuel Compensation Map (16x16) — This map will directly trim Base Fuel Schedule. Given how we have transient throttle fuel compensation maps, this map is really designed for steady state conditions with little RPM deviance. However, you can use this map to tune for transient conditions. View it similarly to STFT's in a way. But as a preset trimming value rather than reacting to AFR deviances. | 16×16 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Main |
| 0x79FD | Target AFR Map (8x8) — This map will be directly influence fueling. Any cells that are set to 14.7 AFR will have the ECU run in closed-loop mode. (Obviously excluding decel) This map will not guarantee that your targets are hit, so you will need to adjust your fueling elsewhere to ensure you're hitting your targets. | 8×8 uint8 | Target AFR (Gasoline Scale), value = 1881.6/x | Fuel Delivery / Air Fuel Ratio / Main |
| 0x7B3D | Intake Cam Timing Map (16x16) — Advance of the intake camshaft in degrees. | 16×16 uint8 | Degrees, value = (x-128)*0.5 | Variable Valve Timing / Main |
| 0x7C3D | Cold Intake Cam Timing Map (8x8) — Cold Intake Cam Timing map. | 8×8 uint8 | Degrees, value = (x-128)*0.5 | Variable Valve Timing / Main |
| 0x7CED | Misfire Diagnosis Map A | 16×16 uint8 | -, raw value | Ignition Timing / Misfire Detection / Main |
| 0x7DED | Misfire Diagnosis Map B | 16×16 uint8 | -, raw value | Ignition Timing / Misfire Detection / Main |
| 0x7EED | Misfire Diagnosis Basic Map — "Misfire Diagnosis table" | 16×16 uint8 | -, raw value | Ignition Timing / Misfire Detection / Main |
| 0x8088 | AFR Correction Map (Bank 1) — This value is added on top of the AFR value from the AFR Conversion Table. | 8×8 uint16 | AFR Adjustment (AFR), value = (x*0.002)-65.536 | Diagnostics / Oxygen Sensor Calibration / Wideband O2 Sensor / Main |
| 0x8108 | AFR Correction Map (Bank 2) — This value is added on top of the AFR value from the AFR Conversion Table. | 8×8 uint16 | AFR Adjustment (AFR), value = (x*0.002)-65.536 | Diagnostics / Oxygen Sensor Calibration / Wideband O2 Sensor / Main |
| 0x8708 | QH0/ Torque Conversion Map — Directly influences throttle opening. | 16×16 uint16 | Requested Torque (lb-ft), value = x*0.073756-2416.836136 | Electronic Throttle Control / Main |
| 0x8C08 | TTEPTD Torque Compensation Map — This map acts as a multiplier for the QH0 Torque Conversion Map value. If the multiplied value exceeds the last column value of the QH0 map, then it'll just use the last column value of the QH0 map instead. | 8×8 uint16 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.0030518 | Electronic Throttle Control / Main |
| 0x8C88 | Engine Torque Map — Map value is compensated, then sent to the TCM for it to determine proper line pressure. Raising the values will result in increased line pressure, while decreasing the values will result in decreased line pressure. It's important to ensure that the map values are at LEAST equal to actual torque output. While it's safe to specify higher torque figures than what you're making, it's extremely dangerous to specify lower torque figures than what you're making. | 16×16 uint16 | Engine Torque (lb-ft), value = x*0.073756-2416.836136 | Transmission / Shifting Performance |

| 0x1400 | Checksum SUM word | uint32 | nisckfix recomputes this after any edit | Checksum |
| 0x1404 | Checksum XOR word | uint32 | nisckfix recomputes this after any edit | Checksum |
| 0x652D | Fuel Injector Latency Adder — This is the value in milliseconds that is added to the injector latency 14V table for every 1v drop in voltage. IE: if latency at 14v is 2ms and the adder is 1ms then the latency at 13v would be 3ms. | 1 uint8 | ms/V, value = x*0.000976563 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x6740 | Closed Loop to Open Loop Delay — "All the delay stage delays" This value represents a maximum delay between the time the car goes from closed to open loop fuel target values. There are several other potential delays but setting this to 0 should override them. For performance applications to ensure that the ecu transitions to the fuel target as fast as possible upon wide open throttle, set to 0. | 1 uint8 | Seconds, value = x*0.2 | Fuel Delivery / Air Fuel Ratio / Delays |
| 0x691F | MAF Factor — Used in main fuel calc, can be used instead of adjusting K factor. This is what Nissan uses to scale MAF from factory. | 1 uint8 | scaling "kg/hr (x*0.0001)" | Airflow / Main |
| 0x6B40 | Fuel Injector Latency at 14V | 1 uint8 | ms, value = x*0.01 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x6C18 | Speed Limiter (Fuel Cut) — Primarily used in automatics. It's the speed at which fuel cut will occur. It's normally set above the throttle cut speed limiter, so you're unlikely to ever hit this stock. | 1 uint8 | Vehicle Speed (MPH), value = x*1.24300808 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x6C24 | Speed Limiter (Fuel Restore) — Ensure that this value is below the fuel cut speed limiter's value. | 1 uint8 | Vehicle Speed (MPH), value = x*1.24300808 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x6DC0 | APO Threshold (Brake) — The APO threshold you need to breach in order to trigger the TVO limiter when the brake is currently being applied. Raising this threshold above ~83 degrees will allow you to bypass this TVO limiter. | 1 uint16 | Degrees, value = x*0.11 | Electronic Throttle Control / Accelerator Pedal / Limiters |
| 0x6F24 | K-Value — Air volume pulse width conversion constant. Represents a fuel injector factor. | 1 uint16 | ms/kg, raw value | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x6FA8 | Rev Limit (Fuel Cut - 3D) — These are the engine speeds at which the fuel cut rev limiter is engaged and disengaged. When engine speed is equal to or exceeds the 'On' value, fuel cut is active, after which, if engine speed drops below the 'Off' value, fueling is resumed. | 2×2 uint16 | Engine Speed (RPM), value = x*12.5 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Cut / Main |
| 0x7036 | Throttle Rev Limiter — Engine speed at which the throttle rev limiter is engaged and disengaged. | 1 uint16 | RPM, value = x*0.78125 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x705E | Speed Limiter — The speed at which throttle cut occurs. For automatics, be sure to change the fuel cut speed limiters as well. | 1 uint16 | MPH, value = x*0.0621371 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x707C | Minimum Injector Pulse Width — This is the minimum pulsewidth the injectors will run at. (Excluding fuel cut) | 1 uint16 | ms, value = x*0.00390625 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x70A8 | Cylinder Filling Up Efficiency Scaler — BFS at which maximum airflow occurs. This value is used to setup ITAC as an estimated Volumetric Efficiency value. So if BFS=BFS Scaler, Cylinder Filling Up Efficiency = 100%. This CAN go above 100%, so ensure that you're never going over this value by too much. | 1 uint16 | ms, value = x*0.000488281 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x70F0 | MAF Idle Voltage Limits — This is the voltage range the ECU expects to see from the MAF sensor at idle. | 2 uint16 | V, value = x*0.005 | Idle Speed Control / Limiters / General Limiters |
| 0x71EC | Checksum XOR word | uint32 | nisckfix recomputes this after any edit | Checksum |
| 0x71F4 | Checksum SUM word | uint32 | nisckfix recomputes this after any edit | Checksum |
| 0x730D | Cold Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when coolant temperature hasn't breached the proper threshold. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x730D | Cold Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x740D | High Octane Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when high-octane fuel is determined. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x740D | High Octane Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x750D | High Detonation Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when high-detonation is occurring. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. Make sure that this map's values are lower than the high octane map's values. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x750D | High Detonation Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x768D | MBT Flame Speed Map — Laminar flow flame velocity basic map | 4×4 uint8 | Laminar Flame Speed (cc/ms), value = x*0.0625 | Ignition Timing / MBT Calculation |
| 0x769D | Cylinder Fresh Air Rate Map — "Fresh Air Rate Map" OR "Freshness Ratio Map". Sets wvITAN (and vITAN), which is used in MBT calculations. | 4×4 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Ignition Timing / MBT Calculation |
| 0x76AD | Acceleration Fuel Compensation Map — Multiplied by mVOLR, Engine RPM, and 55 (unscaled) to set vCFL "FLOAD Basic Value" | 8×8 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Transient Correction |
| 0x76ED | Deceleration Fuel Compensation Map — Multiplied by mVOLR, Engine RPM, and 55 (unscaled) to set vCFL "FLOAD Basic Value" | 8×8 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Transient Correction |
| 0x786D | Fuel Compensation Map (16x16) — This map will directly trim Base Fuel Schedule. Given how we have transient throttle fuel compensation maps, this map is really designed for steady state conditions with little RPM deviance. However, you can use this map to tune for transient conditions. View it similarly to STFT's in a way. But as a preset trimming value rather than reacting to AFR deviances. | 16×16 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Main |
| 0x79FD | Target AFR Map (8x8) — This map will be directly influence fueling. Any cells that are set to 14.7 AFR will have the ECU run in closed-loop mode. (Obviously excluding decel) This map will not guarantee that your targets are hit, so you will need to adjust your fueling elsewhere to ensure you're hitting your targets. | 8×8 uint8 | Target AFR (Gasoline Scale), value = 1881.6/x | Fuel Delivery / Air Fuel Ratio / Main |
| 0x7B3D | Intake Cam Timing Map (16x16) — Advance of the intake camshaft in degrees. | 16×16 uint8 | Degrees, value = (x-128)*0.5 | Variable Valve Timing / Main |
| 0x7C3D | Cold Intake Cam Timing Map (8x8) — Cold Intake Cam Timing map. | 8×8 uint8 | Degrees, value = (x-128)*0.5 | Variable Valve Timing / Main |
| 0x7CED | Misfire Diagnosis Map A | 16×16 uint8 | -, raw value | Ignition Timing / Misfire Detection / Main |
| 0x7DED | Misfire Diagnosis Map B | 16×16 uint8 | -, raw value | Ignition Timing / Misfire Detection / Main |
| 0x7EED | Misfire Diagnosis Basic Map — "Misfire Diagnosis table" | 16×16 uint8 | -, raw value | Ignition Timing / Misfire Detection / Main |
| 0x8088 | AFR Correction Map (Bank 1) — This value is added on top of the AFR value from the AFR Conversion Table. | 8×8 uint16 | AFR Adjustment (AFR), value = (x*0.002)-65.536 | Diagnostics / Oxygen Sensor Calibration / Wideband O2 Sensor / Main |
| 0x8108 | AFR Correction Map (Bank 2) — This value is added on top of the AFR value from the AFR Conversion Table. | 8×8 uint16 | AFR Adjustment (AFR), value = (x*0.002)-65.536 | Diagnostics / Oxygen Sensor Calibration / Wideband O2 Sensor / Main |
| 0x8708 | QH0/ Torque Conversion Map — Directly influences throttle opening. | 16×16 uint16 | Requested Torque (lb-ft), value = x*0.073756-2416.836136 | Electronic Throttle Control / Main |
| 0x8C08 | TTEPTD Torque Compensation Map — This map acts as a multiplier for the QH0 Torque Conversion Map value. If the multiplied value exceeds the last column value of the QH0 map, then it'll just use the last column value of the QH0 map instead. | 8×8 uint16 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.0030518 | Electronic Throttle Control / Main |
| 0x8C88 | Engine Torque Map — Map value is compensated, then sent to the TCM for it to determine proper line pressure. Raising the values will result in increased line pressure, while decreasing the values will result in decreased line pressure. It's important to ensure that the map values are at LEAST equal to actual torque output. While it's safe to specify higher torque figures than what you're making, it's extremely dangerous to specify lower torque figures than what you're making. | 16×16 uint16 | Engine Torque (lb-ft), value = x*0.073756-2416.836136 | Transmission / Shifting Performance |
| 0x8E88 | Knock Slice Map — This table sets the thresholds for determining knock by cylinder. If the knock strength value exceeds this map value, then it adds one to the knock count. For built motors, you'll need to raise these values so that it doesn't count false knock as actual knock. | 16×6 uint16 | Knock Strength Threshold (%), value = x*0.0015259 | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Thresholds |

| 0x9316 | Neutral Idle Ignition Timing Addition Table | 1 uint8 |  |  |
| 0x93AE | Cranking Ignition Timing Table — Cranking Advance Table. | 8 uint8 | Degrees, raw value | Engine Start Performance / Cranking Control / Ignition Timing |
| 0x9526 | Cold Idle Ignition Timing Table — Ignition timing during idle/deceleration. Used when coolant temperature is below mGOVTW's value. (Stock = 131*F) | 8 uint8 | Degrees, value = x-128 | Idle Speed Control / Ignition Timing / GOV Control |
| 0x952E | Idle Ignition Timing Table — Ignition timing during idle/deceleration. During idle/deceleration, the calculated MBT ignition system is not in use. Instead, the ECU uses the GOV Table as the base timing and applies compensations on top of it (Ignition Timing Maps don't affect it). | 8 uint8 | Degrees, value = x-128 | Idle Speed Control / Ignition Timing / GOV Control |
| 0x9536 | Lean Burn Idle Ignition Timing Table — Ignition timing during idle/deceleration. Used exclusively for lean burn engines. | 8 uint8 | Degrees, value = x-128 | Idle Speed Control / Ignition Timing / GOV Control |
| 0x96BE | High Coolant Temperature Increase Compensation Table — A high coolant temperature increase compensation table// Function: Correction Factor for Fuel Addition at High Coolant Temperature/ KHOT | 8 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Engine Cooling |
| 0x974E | Target AFR Table (High Detonation) — This Target AFR table will be used when knock is detected. It will utilize both the Target AFR Table and this Target AFR table to calculate the fueling. It's probably safe to leave this one how it is. | 8 uint8 | Target AFR (Gasoline Scale), value = 1881.6/x | Fuel Delivery / Air Fuel Ratio / Main |
| 0x9848 | Bosch Fuel Cut Table — "BOSCH cut speed table" This is the fuel cut table used for Bosch ECU's only. If the RPM's are above the cut speed, then fuel cut will occur (on decel) until the RPM's hit the recover speed. | 16 uint8 | Engine Speed (RPM), value = x*25 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Cut / Main |
| 0x987C | JECS Fuel Cut Table — "JECS cut speed table" This is the fuel cut table used for JECS/Hitachi ECU's only. | 0x988C | Target Idle RPM Table — Sets the idle RPM that the ECU will attempt to hit. | 16 uint8 | Target Idle Speed (RPM), value = x*12.5 | Idle Speed Control / PID Control / Main |
| 0x98F4 | JECS Fuel Restore Table — "JECS cut recover speed table" This is the recover speed table for JECS/Hitachi fuel cut. | 16 uint8 | Engine Speed (RPM), value = x*25 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Cut / Main |
| 0x99B0 | Bosch Fuel Restore Table — "BOSCH cut recover rotation table" This is the recover speed table for the Bosch fuel cut. | 16 uint8 | Engine Speed (RPM), value = x*25 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Cut / Main |
| 0x99E4 | Individual Cylinder Fuel Trims — "Compensation value table by the cylinder". This adds or subtracts fuel from the respective cylinder. Values over 100 add fuel, values under 100 subtract fuel. | 6 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Main |
| 0x9C02 | Initial Retard Quantity Table (Lock-Up) — Only used when accelerating during lock-up. | 4 uint8 | Degrees, raw value | Ignition Timing / Transient Correction / Main |
| 0x9C06 | Initial Retard Quantity Table — Used when accelerating. | 4 uint8 | Degrees, raw value | Ignition Timing / Transient Correction / Main |
| 0x9C0A | Initial Retard Quantity Table (Idle) | 1 uint8 |  |  |

| 0x740D | High Octane Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when high-octane fuel is determined. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x740D | High Octane Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x750D | High Detonation Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when high-detonation is occurring. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. Make sure that this map's values are lower than the high octane map's values. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x750D | High Detonation Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x768D | MBT Flame Speed Map — Laminar flow flame velocity basic map | 4×4 uint8 | Laminar Flame Speed (cc/ms), value = x*0.0625 | Ignition Timing / MBT Calculation |

| 0x76AD | Acceleration Fuel Compensation Map — Multiplied by mVOLR, Engine RPM, and 55 (unscaled) to set vCFL "FLOAD Basic Value" | 8×8 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Transient Correction |
| 0x76ED | Deceleration Fuel Compensation Map — Multiplied by mVOLR, Engine RPM, and 55 (unscaled) to set vCFL "FLOAD Basic Value" | 8×8 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Transient Correction |
| 0x786D | Fuel Compensation Map (16x16) — This map will directly trim Base Fuel Schedule. However, you can use this map to tune for transient conditions. View it similarly to STFT's in a way. | 0x652D | Fuel Injector Latency Adder — This is the value in milliseconds that is added to the injector latency 14V table for every 1v drop in voltage. | 0x652D | Fuel Injector Latency Adder — This is the value in milliseconds that is added to the injector latency 14V table for every 1v drop in voltage. | 0x6740 | Closed Loop to Open Loop Delay — "All the delay stage delays" This value represents a maximum delay between the time the car goes from closed to open loop fuel target values. There are several other potential delays but setting this to 0 should override them. For performance applications to ensure that the ecu transitions to the fuel target as fast as possible upon wide open throttle, set to 0. | 1 uint8 | Seconds, value = x*0.2 | Fuel Delivery / Air Fuel Ratio / Delays |
| 0x691F | MAF Factor — Used in main fuel calc, can be used instead of adjusting K factor. This is what Nissan uses to scale MAF from factory. | 1 uint8 | scaling "kg/hr (x*0.0001)" | Airflow / Main |

| 0x6C24 | Speed Limiter (Fuel Restore) — Ensure that this value is below the fuel cut speed limiter's value. | 1 uint8 | Vehicle Speed (MPH), value = x*1.24300808 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x6DC0 | APO Threshold (Brake) — The APO threshold you need to breach in order to trigger the TVO limiter when the brake is currently being applied. | 0x730D | Cold Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when coolant temperature hasn't breached the proper threshold. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x730D | Cold Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x740D | High Octane Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when high-octane fuel is determined. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x740D | High Octane Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x750D | High Detonation Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when high-detonation is occurring. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. Make sure that this map's values are lower than the high octane map's values. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x750D | High Detonation Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |

However, you can use this map to tune for transient conditions. View it similarly to STFT's in a way. | 0x652D | Fuel Injector Latency Adder — This is the value in milliseconds that is added to the injector latency 14V table for every 1v drop in voltage. IE: if latency at 14v is 2ms and the adder is 1ms then the latency at 13v would be 3ms. | 1 uint8 | ms/V, value = x*0.000976563 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x6740 | Closed Loop to Open Loop Delay — "All the delay stage delays" This value represents a maximum delay between the time the car goes from closed to open loop fuel target values. There are several other potential delays but setting this to 0 should override them. For performance applications to ensure that the ecu transitions to the fuel target as fast as possible upon wide open throttle, set to 0. | 1 uint8 | Seconds, value = x*0.2 | Fuel Delivery / Air Fuel Ratio / Delays |
| 0x691F | MAF Factor — Used in main fuel calc, can be used instead of adjusting K factor. This is what Nissan uses to scale MAF from factory. | 1 uint8 | scaling "kg/hr (x*0.0001)" | Airflow / Main |

It's normally set above the throttle cut speed limiter, so you're unlikely to ever hit this stock. | 1 uint8 | Vehicle Speed (MPH), value = x*1.24300808 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x6C24 | Speed Limiter (Fuel Restore) — Ensure that this value is below the fuel cut speed limiter's value. | 1 uint8 | Vehicle Speed (MPH), value = x*1.24300808 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x6DC0 | APO Threshold (Brake) — The APO threshold you need to breach in order to trigger the TVO limiter when the brake is currently being applied. Raising this threshold above ~83 degrees will allow you to bypass this TVO limiter. | 1 uint16 | Degrees, value = x*0.11 | Electronic Throttle Control / Accelerator Pedal / Limiters |

| 0x6FA8 | Rev Limit (Fuel Cut - 3D) — These are the engine speeds at which the fuel cut rev limiter is engaged and disengaged. When engine speed is equal to or exceeds the 'On' value, fuel cut is active, after which, if engine speed drops below the 'Off' value, fueling is resumed. | 2×2 uint16 | Engine Speed (RPM), value = x*12.5 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Cut / Main |

| 0x70A8 | Cylinder Filling Up Efficiency Scaler — BFS at which maximum airflow occurs. This value is used to setup ITAC as an estimated Volumetric Efficiency value. So if BFS=BFS Scaler, Cylinder Filling Up Efficiency = 100%. This CAN go above 100%, so ensure that you're never going over this value by too much. | 1 uint16 | ms, value = x*0.000488281 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |

| 0x730D | Cold Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when coolant temperature hasn't breached the proper threshold. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x730D | Cold Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x740D | High Octane Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when high-octane fuel is determined. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x740D | High Octane Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x750D | High Detonation Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when high-detonation is occurring. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. Make sure that this map's values are lower than the high octane map's values. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x750D | High Detonation Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x768D | MBT Flame Speed Map — Laminar flow flame velocity basic map | 4×4 uint8 | Laminar Flame Speed (cc/ms), value = x*0.0625 | Ignition Timing / MBT Calculation |
| 0x769D | Cylinder Fresh Air Rate Map — "Fresh Air Rate Map" OR "Freshness Ratio Map". Sets wvITAN (and vITAN), which is used in MBT calculations. | 4×4 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Ignition Timing / MBT Calculation |
| 0x76AD | Acceleration Fuel Compensation Map — Multiplied by mVOLR, Engine RPM, and 55 (unscaled) to set vCFL "FLOAD Basic Value" | 8×8 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Transient Correction |
| 0x76ED | Deceleration Fuel Compensation Map — Multiplied by mVOLR, Engine RPM, and 55 (unscaled) to set vCFL "FLOAD Basic Value" | 8×8 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Transient Correction |
| 0x786D | Fuel Compensation Map (16x16) — This map will directly trim Base Fuel Schedule. Given how we have transient throttle fuel compensation maps, this map is really designed for steady state conditions with little RPM deviance. However, you can use this map to tune for transient conditions. View it similarly to STFT's in a way. But as a preset trimming value rather than reacting to AFR deviances. | 16×16 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Main |
| 0x79FD | Target AFR Map (8x8) — This map will be directly influence fueling. Any cells that are set to 14.7 AFR will have the ECU run in closed-loop mode. (Obviously excluding decel) This map will not guarantee that your targets are hit, so you will need to adjust your fueling elsewhere to ensure you're hitting your targets. | 8×8 uint8 | Target AFR (Gasoline Scale), value = 1881.6/x | Fuel Delivery / Air Fuel Ratio / Main |
| 0x7B3D | Intake Cam Timing Map (16x16) — Advance of the intake camshaft in degrees. | 16×16 uint8 | Degrees, value = (x-128)*0.5 | Variable Valve Timing / Main |
| 0x7C3D | Cold Intake Cam Timing Map (8x8) — Cold Intake Cam Timing map. | 8×8 uint8 | Degrees, value = (x-128)*0.5 | Variable Valve Timing / Main |
| 0x7CED | Misfire Diagnosis Basic Map — "Misfire Diagnosis table" | 16×16 uint8 | -, raw value | Ignition Timing / Misfire Detection / Main |

| 0x7EED | Misfire Diagnosis Map A | 16×16 uint8 | -, raw value | Ignition Timing / Misfire Detection / Main |

| 0x8108 | AFR Correction Map (Bank 2) — This value is added on top of the AFR value from the AFR Conversion Table. | 8×8 uint16 | AFR Adjustment (AFR), value = (x*0.002)-65.536 | Diagnostics / Oxygen Sensor Calibration / Wideband O2 Sensor / Main |

If the multiplied value exceeds the last column value of the QH0 map, then it'll just use the last column value of the QH0 map instead. | 8×8 uint16 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.0030518 | Electronic Throttle Control / Main |
| 0x8C88 | Engine Torque Map — Map value is compensated, then sent to the TCM for it to determine proper line pressure. Raising the values will result in increased line pressure, while decreasing the values will result in decreased line pressure. It's important to ensure that the map values are at LEAST equal to actual torque output. While it's safe to specify higher torque figures than what you're making, it's extremely dangerous to specify lower torque figures than what you're making. | 16×16 uint16 | Engine Torque (lb-ft), value = x*0.073756-2416.836136 | Transmission / Shifting Performance |

| 0x6CE6 | Fuel Injector Latency Adder — This is the value in milliseconds that is added to the injector latency 14V table for every 1v drop in voltage. IE: if latency at 14v is 2ms and the adder is 1ms then the latency at 13v would be 3ms. | 1 uint8 | ms/V, value = x*0.000976563 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x6F42 | Closed Loop to Open Loop Delay — "All the delay stage delays" This value represents a maximum delay between the time the car goes from closed to open loop fuel target values. There are several other potential delays but setting this to 0 should override them. For performance applications to ensure that the ecu transitions to the fuel target as fast as possible upon wide open throttle, set to 0. | 1 uint8 | Seconds, value = x*0.2 | Fuel Delivery / Air Fuel Ratio / Delays |
| 0x715A | MAF Factor — Used in main fuel calc, can be used instead of adjusting K factor. This is what Nissan uses to scale MAF from factory. | 1 uint8 | scaling "kg/hr (x*0.0001)" | Airflow / Main |
| 0x7398 | Fuel Injector Latency at 14V | 1 uint8 | ms, value = x*0.01 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x7492 | Speed Limiter (Fuel Cut) — Primarily used in automatics. It's the speed at which fuel cut will occur. It's normally set above the throttle cut speed limiter, so you're unlikely to ever hit this stock. | 1 uint8 | Vehicle Speed (MPH), value = x*1.24300808 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x749E | Speed Limiter (Fuel Restore) — Ensure that this value is below the fuel cut speed limiter's value. | 1 uint8 | Vehicle Speed (MPH), value = x*1.24300808 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x767C | APO Threshold (Brake) — The APO threshold you need to breach in order to trigger the TVO limiter when the brake is currently being applied. Raising this threshold above ~83 degrees will allow you to bypass this TVO limiter. | 1 uint16 | Degrees, value = x*0.11 | Electronic Throttle Control / Accelerator Pedal / Limiters |
| 0x7814 | K-Value — Air volume pulse width conversion constant. Represents a fuel injector factor. | 1 uint16 | ms/kg, raw value | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x78A6 | Rev Limit (Fuel Cut - 3D) — These are the engine speeds at which the fuel cut rev limiter is engaged and disengaged. When engine speed is equal to or exceeds the 'On' value, fuel cut is active, after which, if engine speed drops below the 'Off' value, fueling is resumed. | 2×2 uint16 | Engine Speed (RPM), value = x*12.5 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Cut / Main |
| 0x793E | Throttle Rev Limiter — Engine speed at which the throttle rev limiter is engaged and disengaged. | 1 uint16 | RPM, value = x*0.78125 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x7970 | Speed Limiter — The speed at which throttle cut occurs. For automatics, be sure to change the fuel cut speed limiters as well. | 1 uint16 | MPH, value = x*0.0621371 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x79CE | Minimum Injector Pulse Width — This is the minimum pulsewidth the injectors will run at. (Excluding fuel cut) | 1 uint16 | ms, value = x*0.00390625 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x79FC | Cylinder Filling Up Efficiency Scaler — BFS at which maximum airflow occurs. This value is used to setup ITAC as an estimated Volumetric Efficiency value. So if BFS=BFS Scaler, Cylinder Filling Up Efficiency = 100%. This CAN go above 100%, so ensure that you're never going over this value by too much. | 1 uint16 | ms, value = x*0.000488281 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x7A4C | MAF Idle Voltage Limits — This is the voltage range the ECU expects to see from the MAF sensor at idle. | 2 uint16 | V, value = x*0.005 | Idle Speed Control / Limiters / General Limiters |

| 0x7CAD | Cold Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when coolant temperature hasn't breached the proper threshold. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x7CAD | Cold Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x7DAD | High Octane Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when high-octane fuel is determined. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x7DAD | High Octane Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x7EAD | High Detonation Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when high-detonation is occurring. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. Make sure that this map's values are lower than the high octane map's values. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x7EAD | High Detonation Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x806D | MBT Flame Speed Map — Laminar flow flame velocity basic map | 4×4 uint8 | Laminar Flame Speed (cc/ms), value = x*0.0625 | Ignition Timing / MBT Calculation |
| 0x807D | Cylinder Fresh Air Rate Map — "Fresh Air Rate Map" OR "Freshness Ratio Map". Sets wvITAN (and vITAN), which is used in MBT calculations. | 4×4 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Ignition Timing / MBT Calculation |
| 0x808D | Acceleration Fuel Compensation Map — Multiplied by mVOLR, Engine RPM, and 55 (unscaled) to set vCFL "FLOAD Basic Value" | 8×8 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Transient Correction |
| 0x80CD | Deceleration Fuel Compensation Map — Multiplied by mVOLR, Engine RPM, and 55 (unscaled) to set vCFL "FLOAD Basic Value" | 8×8 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Transient Correction |
| 0x834D | Fuel Compensation Map (16x16) — This map will directly trim Base Fuel Schedule. Given how we have transient throttle fuel compensation maps, this map is really designed for steady state conditions with little RPM deviance. However, you can use this map to tune for transient conditions. View it similarly to STFT's in a way. But as a preset trimming value rather than reacting to AFR deviances. | 16×16 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Main |
| 0x85DD | Target AFR Map (8x8) — This map will be directly influence fueling. Any cells that are set to 14.7 AFR will have the ECU run in closed-loop mode. (Obviously excluding decel) This map will not guarantee that your targets are hit, so you will need to adjust your fueling elsewhere to ensure you're hitting your targets. | 8×8 uint8 | Target AFR (Gasoline Scale), value = 1881.6/x | Fuel Delivery / Air Fuel Ratio / Main |
| 0x89ED | Intake Cam Timing Map (16x16) — Advance of the intake camshaft in degrees. | 16×16 uint8 | Degrees, value = (x-128)*0.5 | Variable Valve Timing / Main |
| 0x8AED | Cold Intake Cam Timing Map (8x8) — Cold Intake Cam Timing map. | 8×8 uint8 | Degrees, value = (x-128)*0.5 | Variable Valve Timing / Main |
| 0x8BBD | Misfire Diagnosis Map A | 16×16 uint8 | -, raw value | Ignition Timing / Misfire Detection / Main |
| 0x8CBD | Misfire Diagnosis Map B | 16×16 uint8 | -, raw value | Ignition Timing / Misfire Detection / Main |
| 0x8DBD | Misfire Diagnosis Basic Map — "Misfire Diagnosis table" | 16×16 uint8 | -, raw value | Ignition Timing / Misfire Detection / Main |
| 0x8F58 | AFR Correction Map (Bank 1) — This value is added on top of the AFR value from the AFR Conversion Table. | 8×8 uint16 | AFR Adjustment (AFR), value = (x*0.002)-65.536 | Diagnostics / Oxygen Sensor Calibration / Wideband O2 Sensor / Main |
| 0x8FD8 | AFR Correction Map (Bank 2) — This value is added on top of the AFR value from the AFR Conversion Table. | 8×8 uint16 | AFR Adjustment (AFR), value = (x*0.002)-65.536 | Diagnostics / Oxygen Sensor Calibration / Wideband O2 Sensor / Main |
| 0x9658 | QH0/ Torque Conversion Map — Directly influences throttle opening. | 16×16 uint16 | Requested Torque (lb-ft), value = x*0.073756-2416.836136 | Electronic Throttle Control / Main |
| 0x9D58 | TTEPTD Torque Compensation Map — This map acts as a multiplier for the QH0 Torque Conversion Map value. If the multiplied value exceeds the last column value of the QH0 map, then it'll just use the last column value of the QH0 map instead. | 8×8 uint16 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.0030518 | Electronic Throttle Control / Main |
| 0x9DD8 | Engine Torque Map — Map value is compensated, then sent to the TCM for it to determine proper line pressure. Raising the values will result in increased line pressure, while decreasing the values will result in decreased line pressure. It's important to ensure that the map values are at LEAST equal to actual torque output. While it's safe to specify higher torque figures than what you're making, it's extremely dangerous to specify lower torque figures than what you're making. | 16×16 uint16 | Engine Torque (lb-ft), value = x*0.073756-2416.836136 | Transmission / Shifting Performance |
| 0x9FD8 | Knock Slice Map — This table sets the thresholds for determining knock by cylinder. If the knock strength value exceeds this map value, then it adds one to the knock count. For built motors, you'll need to raise these values so that it doesn't count false knock as actual knock. | 16×6 uint16 | Knock Strength Threshold (%), value = x*0.0015259 | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Thresholds |

| 0xA4FA | Neutral Idle Ignition Timing Addition Table | 1 uint8 |  |  |

| 0xA736 | Idle Ignition Timing Table — Ignition timing during idle/deceleration. During idle/deceleration, the calculated MBT ignition system is not in use. | 0xA73E | Lean Burn Idle Ignition Timing Table — Ignition timing during idle/deceleration. Used exclusively for lean burn engines. | 8 uint8 | Degrees, value = x-128 | Idle Speed Control / Ignition Timing / GOV Control |

| 0xA95A | High Coolant Temperature Increase Compensation Table — A high coolant temperature increase compensation table// Function: Correction Factor for Fuel Addition at High Coolant Temperature/ KHOT | 8 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Engine Cooling |
| 0xAA42 | Target AFR Table (High Detonation) — This Target AFR table will be used when knock is detected. It will utilize both the Target AFR Table and this Target AFR table to calculate the fueling. It's probably safe to leave this one how it is. | 8 uint8 | Target AFR (Gasoline Scale), value = 1881.6/x | Fuel Delivery / Air Fuel Ratio / Main |

| 0xAB78 | JECS Fuel Cut Table — "JECS cut speed table" This is the fuel cut table used for JECS/Hitachi ECU's only. | 0xAB88 | Target Idle RPM Table — Sets the idle RPM that the ECU will attempt to hit. | 16 uint8 | Target Idle Speed (RPM), value = x*12.5 | Idle Speed Control / PID Control / Main |

| Address | Controls | Layout | Values mean | Category |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x6D38 | Fuel Injector Latency Adder — This is the value in milliseconds that is added to the injector latency 14V table for every 1v drop in voltage. IE: if latency at 14v is 2ms and the adder is 1ms then the latency at 13v would be 3ms. | 1 uint8 | ms/V, value = x*0.000976563 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x6F97 | Closed Loop to Open Loop Delay — "All the delay stage delays" This value represents a maximum delay between the time the car goes from closed to open loop fuel target values. There are several other potential delays but setting this to 0 should override them. For performance applications to ensure that the ecu transitions to the fuel target as fast as possible upon wide open throttle, set to 0. | 1 uint8 | Seconds, value = x*0.2 | Fuel Delivery / Air Fuel Ratio / Delays |
| 0x70D9 | O2 Sensor Position Flags — Controls what O2 sensors the ECU thinks it has. Disabling any of them will cause said sensor to no longer be utilized by the ECU. (MIGHT need to force emission readiness, as it'll probably show "not supported" for catalyst monitoring) | 1 uint8 |  | Options / Flags |
| 0x71B4 | MAF Factor — Used in main fuel calc, can be used instead of adjusting K factor. This is what Nissan uses to scale MAF from factory. | 1 uint8 | scaling "kg/hr (x*0.0001)" | Airflow / Main |
| 0x7214 | Radiator Fan Switch Point | 1 uint8 |  |  |
| 0x73F5 | Fuel Injector Latency at 14V | 1 uint8 | ms, value = x*0.01 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x74F0 | Speed Limiter (Fuel Cut) — Primarily used in automatics. It's the speed at which fuel cut will occur. It's normally set above the throttle cut speed limiter, so you're unlikely to ever hit this stock. | 1 uint8 | Vehicle Speed (MPH), value = x*1.24300808 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x74FC | Speed Limiter (Fuel Restore) — Ensure that this value is below the fuel cut speed limiter's value. | 1 uint8 | Vehicle Speed (MPH), value = x*1.24300808 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x76EE | APO Threshold (Brake) — The APO threshold you need to breach in order to trigger the TVO limiter when the brake is currently being applied. Raising this threshold above ~83 degrees will allow you to bypass this TVO limiter. | 1 uint16 | Degrees, value = x*0.11 | Electronic Throttle Control / Accelerator Pedal / Limiters |
| 0x788A | K-Value — Air volume pulse width conversion constant. Represents a fuel injector factor. | 1 uint16 | ms/kg, raw value | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x791C | Rev Limit (Fuel Cut - 3D) — These are the engine speeds at which the fuel cut rev limiter is engaged and disengaged. When engine speed is equal to or exceeds the 'On' value, fuel cut is active, after which, if engine speed drops below the 'Off' value, fueling is resumed. | 2×2 uint16 | Engine Speed (RPM), value = x*12.5 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Cut / Main |
| 0x79B4 | Throttle Rev Limiter — Engine speed at which the throttle rev limiter is engaged and disengaged. | 1 uint16 | RPM, value = x*0.78125 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x79E6 | Speed Limiter — The speed at which throttle cut occurs. For automatics, be sure to change the fuel cut speed limiters as well. | 1 uint16 | MPH, value = x*0.0621371 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x7A44 | Minimum Injector Pulse Width — This is the minimum pulsewidth the injectors will run at. (Excluding fuel cut) | 1 uint16 | ms, value = x*0.00390625 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x7A74 | Cylinder Filling Up Efficiency Scaler — BFS at which maximum airflow occurs. This value is used to setup ITAC as an estimated Volumetric Efficiency value. So if BFS=BFS Scaler, Cylinder Filling Up Efficiency = 100%. This CAN go above 100%, so ensure that you're never going over this value by too much. | 1 uint16 | ms, value = x*0.000488281 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |

| 0x7BC4 | Checksum XOR word | uint32 | nisckfix recomputes this after any edit | Checksum |
| 0x7BCC | Checksum SUM word | uint32 | nisckfix recomputes this after any edit | Checksum |
| 0x7D65 | Cold Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when coolant temperature hasn't breached the proper threshold. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x7D65 | Cold Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x7E65 | High Octane Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when high-octane fuel is determined. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |

## AC81A · 2005 Infiniti G35 Rev-Up · ECUID 1AC81A · SH7058 · 1024kb

| Address | Controls | Layout | Values mean | Category |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x6D38 | Fuel Injector Latency Adder — This is the value in milliseconds that is added to the injector latency 14V table for every 1v drop in voltage. IE: if latency at 14v is 2ms and the adder is 1ms then the latency at 13v would be 3ms. | 1 uint8 | ms/V, value = x*0.000976563 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x6F97 | Closed Loop to Open Loop Delay — "All the delay stage delays" This value represents a maximum delay between the time the car goes from closed to open loop fuel target values. There are several other potential delays but setting this to 0 should override them. For performance applications to ensure that the ecu transitions to the fuel target as fast as possible upon wide open throttle, set to 0. | 1 uint8 | Seconds, value = x*0.2 | Fuel Delivery / Air Fuel Ratio / Delays |
| 0x70D9 | O2 Sensor Position Flags — Controls what O2 sensors the ECU thinks it has. Disabling any of them will cause said sensor to no longer be utilized by the ECU. (MIGHT need to force emission readiness, as it'll probably show "not supported" for catalyst monitoring) | 1 uint8 |  | Options / Flags |
| 0x71B4 | MAF Factor — Used in main fuel calc, can be used instead of adjusting K factor. This is what Nissan uses to scale MAF from factory. | 1 uint8 | scaling "kg/hr (x*0.0001)" | Airflow / Main |
| 0x7214 | Radiator Fan Switch Point | 1 uint8 |  |  |
| 0x73F5 | Fuel Injector Latency at 14V | 1 uint8 | ms, value = x*0.01 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x74F0 | Speed Limiter (Fuel Cut) — Primarily used in automatics. It's the speed at which fuel cut will occur. It's normally set above the throttle cut speed limiter, so you're unlikely to ever hit this stock. | 1 uint8 | Vehicle Speed (MPH), value = x*1.24300808 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x74FC | Speed Limiter (Fuel Restore) — Ensure that this value is below the fuel cut speed limiter's value. | 1 uint8 | Vehicle Speed (MPH), value = x*1.24300808 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x76EE | APO Threshold (Brake) — The APO threshold you need to breach in order to trigger the TVO limiter when the brake is currently being applied. Raising this threshold above ~83 degrees will allow you to bypass this TVO limiter. | 1 uint16 | Degrees, value = x*0.11 | Electronic Throttle Control / Accelerator Pedal / Limiters |
| 0x788A | K-Value — Air volume pulse width conversion constant. Represents a fuel injector factor. | 1 uint16 | ms/kg, raw value | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x791C | Rev Limit (Fuel Cut - 3D) — These are the engine speeds at which the fuel cut rev limiter is engaged and disengaged. When engine speed is equal to or exceeds the 'On' value, fuel cut is active, after which, if engine speed drops below the 'Off' value, fueling is resumed. | 2×2 uint16 | Engine Speed (RPM), value = x*12.5 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Cut / Main |
| 0x79B4 | Throttle Rev Limiter — Engine speed at which the throttle rev limiter is engaged and disengaged. | 1 uint16 | RPM, value = x*0.78125 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x79E6 | Speed Limiter — The speed at which throttle cut occurs. For automatics, be sure to change the fuel cut speed limiters as well. | 1 uint16 | MPH, value = x*0.0621371 | Diagnostics / Gauge Cluster / Vehicle Speed Control / Speed Limiters |
| 0x7A44 | Minimum Injector Pulse Width — This is the minimum pulsewidth the injectors will run at. (Excluding fuel cut) | 1 uint16 | ms, value = x*0.00390625 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x7A74 | Cylinder Filling Up Efficiency Scaler — BFS at which maximum airflow occurs. This value is used to setup ITAC as an estimated Volumetric Efficiency value. So if BFS=BFS Scaler, Cylinder Filling Up Efficiency = 100%. This CAN go above 100%, so ensure that you're never going over this value by too much. | 1 uint16 | ms, value = x*0.000488281 | Fuel Delivery / Fuel Injector Calibration / Specifications / Main |
| 0x7A88 | Idle BFS Limits — If your BFS at idle exceeds these values, it'll throw a P0507(5 or 607? the ISC one) | 2 uint16 | ms, value = x*0.0005 | Idle Speed Control / Fuel Delivery / Limiters |
| 0x7AC4 | MAF Idle Voltage Limits — This is the voltage range the ECU expects to see from the MAF sensor at idle. | 2 uint16 | V, value = x*0.005 | Idle Speed Control / Limiters / General Limiters |
| 0x7BC4 | Checksum XOR word | uint32 | nisckfix recomputes this after any edit | Checksum |
| 0x7BCC | Checksum SUM word | uint32 | nisckfix recomputes this after any edit | Checksum |
| 0x7D65 | Cold Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when coolant temperature hasn't breached the proper threshold. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x7D65 | Cold Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x7E65 | High Octane Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when high-octane fuel is determined. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x7E65 | High Octane Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x7F65 | High Detonation Ignition Timing Map (16x16) — This is the main trimming map that the ECU uses when high-detonation is occurring. The ECU calculates a MBT ignition advance, then this trimming map value is added/subtracted from that value. However, there are other compensations that occur as well. Make sure that this map's values are lower than the high octane map's values. | 16×16 uint8 | Timing Adjustment (°), value = x-64 | Ignition Timing / Main |
| 0x7F65 | High Detonation Ignition Timing Map Knock Window — This is the knock window that determines whether the ECU will aggressively pull timing if knock is detected. So basically, if you're in the knock window and knock is detected, it'll pull timing and keep timing retarded from MBT for a bit while it waits to see if anymore knock occurs. If no more knock occurs, it'll slowly add timing back. If more knock occurs, it'll continue retarding timing. | 16×16 uint8 | Knock Window (0: Off \| 1: On), raw value | Ignition Timing / Knock Control / Main |
| 0x8125 | MBT Flame Speed Map — Laminar flow flame velocity basic map | 4×4 uint8 | Laminar Flame Speed (cc/ms), value = x*0.0625 | Ignition Timing / MBT Calculation |

| 0x8185 | Deceleration Fuel Compensation Map — Multiplied by mVOLR, Engine RPM, and 55 (unscaled) to set vCFL "FLOAD Basic Value" | 8×8 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Transient Correction |
| 0x8405 | Fuel Compensation Map (16x16) — This map will directly trim Base Fuel Schedule. Given how we have transient throttle fuel compensation maps, this map is really designed for steady state conditions with little RPM deviance. However, you can use this map to tune for transient conditions. View it similarly to STFT's in a way. But as a preset trimming value rather than reacting to AFR deviances. | 16×16 uint8 | Compensation (%), value = x*0.78125 | Fuel Delivery / Main |
